paper_metadata.title: Re Segregation at Interfacial Dislocation Network in a Nickel-Based Superalloy

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: The distribution of Rhenium (Re) in a Ni-based single-crystal superalloy is studied by sub-angstrom resolution transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS).

evidence.section: Abstract
evidence.quote: It is found that Re atoms segregate at the tensile stress regions near the interfacial dislocation cores, forming the “Cottrell atmosphere”, and the segregation process is facilitated by dislocation pipe diffusion.

evidence.section: Abstract

evidence.section: 4. Analysis and discussion
evidence.quote: The strain energy incurred by adding Re is still lowered in comparison to the Re-free system since the majority of Re atoms is concentrated in the core region. In energetics, we found the dislocation energy drops 152.7 eV per nm on average after adding Re, which implies that Re atoms may have a noticeable pinning effect on the dislocation in comparison to the Re-free dislocations.
